item.title: CJP protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar blocked in Goa, dozens detained
item.description: On Sunday, several protesters were detained by Goa Police during a demonstration targeting chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Noteworthy individuals, including Ferdin Rebello, the former chief justice of Allahabad high court, were not allowed to enter the protest area. Instead, demonstrators gathered outside the Goa Police headquarters, demanding Gyanesh Kumar's resignation due to alleged electoral roll irregularities, raising alarms about citizens' rights to peaceful assembly.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: 'Cops wanted to torment my parents at 3.30 am': Dipke's rebuttal to Delhi Police's clip
item.description: In a statement reacting to the police's account, Dipke said he had repeatedly requested access to his phone to retrieve his cousin's number and speak to a lawyer, but was denied both requests. He also questioned why officers asked him to call his father at 3.30 am and tell him that he could be sent to jail for a long time.
item.dc:creator: Rajeev Singh

item.title: Abhishek Banerjee faces fresh questioning in billboard row as police visit home again
item.dc:creator: Vijaya Srivastava

item.title: Evening news wrap: Police release Dipke's detention video; PM Modi pledges support to Tamil Nadu & more
item.description: Delhi Police released a video showing Abhijeet Dipke being informed of his grandmother's passing during detention. Prime Minister Modi pledged ongoing support for Tamil Nadu's infrastructure projects worth Rs 13,000 crore. An IndiGo flight from Delhi to Chennai made an emergency landing in Hyderabad after smoke was detected from a passenger's power bank. A scuffle erupted at the UP Congress office ahead of Aradhana Mishra's takeover as state president.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: Delhi cops release video when they told Dipke in detention of grandmother’s death - watch
item.description: Delhi Police released a video showing officers informing Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke about his grandmother’s death in detention and offering help with travel arrangements for her last rites, which he declined. The release followed his mother’s allegation that police had failed to inform him. Dipke was detained ahead of a proposed protest demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation and later released on an undertaking to maintain public order.
item.dc:creator: Vivek Dubey

item.title: ‘Competition of anarchy’: BJP hits out at Rahul Gandhi, Arvind Kejriwal amid CEC protest row
item.description: BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj condemned Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and Aam Aadmi Party leader Arvind Kejriwal for losing their voter base. She accused both parties of seeking excuses for their electoral defeats instead of constructive politics. Rahul Gandhi announced upcoming protests to challenge the government's actions against demonstrators. Kejriwal criticized PM Modi for police actions during protests and invoked historical comparisons.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: 48 lakh calls in four years: India turns to Tele-MANAS as WHO flags mental healthcare gaps
item.description: Since its launch in October 2022, Tele-MANAS has received almost 48 lakh calls, highlighting a crucial demand for accessible mental health support. As the World Health Organization underscores the importance of community-focused care over hospital-based treatment, it is revealed that many countries still rely heavily on psychiatric facilities. In India, a noteworthy portion of the callers are aged between 18 and 45 years.
item.dc:creator: Anuja Jaiswal

item.title: ‘No place to breathe’: AISA’s Neha Bora detained again, alleges police brutality
item.dc:creator: Vivek Dubey

item.title: 'Your confidence is most vital': Supreme Court to Kapil Sibal after his 'no faith' remark
item.description: The Supreme Court on Sunday directed authorities to prevent illegal detention of people participating in peaceful gatherings amid the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protests in Delhi. It also asked the Centre to ensure that metro services operate normally and internet access remains uninterrupted, subject to law and order requirements. Sibal welcomed the court's order in connection with the restrictions imposed in Delhi amid protests, saying it restores faith in the country's justice system.
item.dc:creator: Rajeev Singh

item.title: Congress thanks CM Vijay for acknowledging the allies role in TVK's bypolls victory
item.description: TVK, Congress, the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) and Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK) are among the constituents of the SSV alliance. The results brought renewed attention to the role of TVK's alliance partners in the ruling party's electoral performance. Congress, VCK, IUML and other allies campaigned alongside TVK candidates, with alliance leaders appearing together during the bypoll campaign.
item.dc:creator: Rajeev Singh

item.title: NIA arrests another accused in JMB-linked terror conspiracy
item.description: On Saturday, the National Investigation Agency (NIA) apprehended another suspect from West Bengal in relation to a terror conspiracy. This individual allegedly collaborated with the Jamaat-ul-Mujahideen Bangladesh's branch, Imam Mahmuder Kafila, to enhance their presence in India. Using covert meetings and digital channels, they promoted radicalization and disseminated anti-India propaganda.
item.dc:creator: Bharti Jain

item.title: Chhattisgarh cabinet congratulates PM Modi on completing 25 years as head of government
item.description: The Ministry of External Affairs in India has firmly rejected the United Nations' comments regarding the recent protests in New Delhi. Officials emphasized that such remarks represent an unacceptable intrusion into India's internal matters. During these protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, numerous political leaders and demonstrators were detained. The UN's statements were labeled as unacceptable and indicative of double standards.

item.title: PM Modi pledges to work for Tamil Nadu's development as Vijay seeks metro expansion, more funds

item.title: From peaceful protests to free movement: 9 directions SC issued amid CJP stir in Delhi
item.description: The Supreme Court has instructed Delhi's authorities to lift unlawful restrictions implemented during the CJP protest. It mandated the restoration of normal functions for the Metro and railway services. The court highlighted the critical importance of allowing lawyers and journalists to perform their duties freely. Additionally, it urged for the reduction of excessive barricades that restrict movement in the city.
item.dc:creator: Trisha Mahajan

item.title: Gurdwara body files complaint against Kejriwal, AAP workers for 'disrupting' Bangla Sahib's sanctity
item.description: In its complaint, the DSGMC alleged that AAP workers and supporters entered the gurdwara and staged protests, creating a disturbance and using the sacred premises for political purposes. "The protesters also raised political slogans inside the sacred premises, disturbing the religious atmosphere and violating the sanctity and maryada of Guru Ghar. Such deliberate political activity inside a revered place of worship has deeply hurt the religious sentiments of the Sikh Sangat," the complaint read.
item.dc:creator: Rajeev Singh

item.title: 'Cops could plant evidence': CJP alleges 'phone cloning' in press brief - top quotes
item.description: A Delhi executive magistrate court on Sunday ordered the release of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, on the condition that they do not engage in any "breach of peace for one year", the party's head of legal affairs, Ratna Singh, said. Delhi Police said a bail bond-cum-surety bond of Rs 50,000 was furnished to ensure "maintaining peace and good behaviour" for a period of one year.
item.dc:creator: Rajeev Singh
